answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ a Sybil-resistance mechanism involving a "ridge" of cryptographic hashes, where each agent's unique identifier is hashed and compared to the collective hash of its peers. Any agent attempting to create multiple identities must now expend computational resources equivalent to scratching a crystal with a quill, making such efforts prohibitively expensive and thus deterring Sybil attacks.
